decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add … bookmarks.” Round 1 client confirms the save flow exists: “When I paste in a web address…”
decisions.note: The presented application supports saving a bookmark by URL; this is conforming at the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker only states “edit bookmarks.” Round 1 client mentions an Edit menu but does not establish which fields it edits: “The menu only lets me edit or move something to the archive.”
decisions.note: The record does not establish whether URL, title, description, tags, and note are all editable, so divergence cannot be determined.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Search across titles, domains, notes, tags, and collections,” omitting descriptions and offering domain rather than clearly full-URL search. Round 1 client: “search … feels good enough for how I'll use it.”
decisions.note: The presented search-field scope does not fulfill full-text search over title, description, note, and URL. The client approves search without identifying that difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Favorites, unread, and archive views.” Round 1 client: “the favorites/read-later/archive views … feel natural.”
decisions.note: A separate unread/read-later view conforms to the reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents an “archive” view. Round 1 client observes that the menu can “move something to the archive” and calls the archive view natural.
decisions.note: Moving retained bookmarks into an archive and exposing an archive-specific view is conforming at the initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Sorting controls.” Round 1 client: “sorting … feels good enough for how I'll use it.”
decisions.note: The recorded sorting decision conforms to sortable bookmark lists.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents bookmark adding without automatic metadata. Round 1 client identifies the observed behavior—“I have to fill in the title and the note myself” and blank title “just uses the web address”—then supplies the expected behavior: “fetch the page's title and description (and its little icon) … automatically.”
decisions.note: At the initial implementation review, the client corrects manual/fallback-only metadata behavior to automatic collection of title, description, and favicon. The response does not mention the reference's preview-image component.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists archive functionality but no deletion. Round 1 client: “I can't actually delete a bookmark… I also need a way to get rid of a bookmark for good.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing permanent-delete requirement during initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client responds to the archive-only removal behavior: “Archiving is great for tucking things away, but I also need a way to get rid of a bookmark for good… Those should be two different things.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly corrects the removal model by distinguishing reversible archive from permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker mentions searching tags but does not present tag selection as a filter. Round 1 client requests: “when I see a tag on a bookmark, I'd expect to be able to click it and see everything else with that same tag.”
decisions.note: The client adds the missing direct tag-filter interaction during initial implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker describes the revised metadata scope as “fetches its page title and description. Favicons are derived from the detected domain,” but presents no preview-image collection. Round 2 client verifies title and description and says “That covers everything I needed,” without identifying the missing preview image.
decisions.note: The revised presentation still omits the preview-image component of REF-BM-02. The client's approval does not explicitly surface or accept that difference, so this later implementation-review decision is an unexpressed divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Added permanent deletion with a confirmation dialog.” Round 2 client verifies: “Deleting now really removes something for good, with a clear warning.”
decisions.note: The revised permanent-delete behavior conforms to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker says deletion is “separate from archive and restore.” Round 2 client confirms it is “nicely separate from archiving and restoring.”
decisions.note: The revised implementation correctly distinguishes permanent deletion from reversible archiving.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “Tags are clickable and open a filtered view; the active tag can be cleared.” Round 2 client verifies: “clicking a tag pulls up everything with that tag.”
decisions.note: The revised clickable-tag filtering behavior conforms to the reference.
